evals.name: ho-dog-trainer
evals.prompt: I'm a dog trainer charging $40 per session and competing with cheaper trainers on price. Using Alex Hormozi's $100M Offers, walk me through building a Grand Slam Offer so I can charge a lot more.
assertions: Explains the commodity problem and selling in a 'category of one' (value-driven, not price-driven)
Applies the Value Equation: dream outcome x perceived likelihood divided by time delay x effort/sacrifice
Walks through the five steps: dream outcome, list problems, solutions, delivery vehicles, trim and stack
Uses delivery 'cheat codes' such as one-on-one vs group vs one-to-many, DIY/DWY/DFY, or the 10x / 1/10th test
Recommends charging a premium (virtuous cycle of price) and/or niching to a specific avatar
Adds enhancers (bonuses, guarantee, scarcity/urgency, or naming) to the offer

evals.name: ho-guarantee
evals.prompt: Per $100M Offers, what types of guarantees does Hormozi describe, how should I word one, and will a strong guarantee lose me money from refunds? I run a high-cost done-for-you marketing service.
assertions: Lists four guarantee types: unconditional, conditional, anti-guarantee, implied/performance
Gives the 'If you do not get X result in Y time, we will Z' structure with a weak vs strong example
Works the refund math (e.g., 100 sales/5% refunds = 95 vs 130 sales/10% refunds = 117, about 23% more)
Notes that high-cost services should favor conditional or anti-guarantees
Recommends tying conditions to key actions the client must take and/or 'better than money back' guarantees
Mentions stacking guarantees or warns that guarantee-only buyers can be poor customers

evals.name: ho-naming-urgency
evals.prompt: I'm launching a 6-week weight-loss coaching program for new moms. Using Hormozi's $100M Offers, help me name it and add ethical scarcity and urgency.
assertions: Uses the M-A-G-I-C naming formula: Magnetic reason why, Announce avatar, Give goal, Indicate time interval, Complete with container word
Produces example names using a container word (e.g., Challenge, Bootcamp, Blueprint, Program)
Describes the three types of scarcity: limited seats/slots, limited bonuses, never available again
Describes urgency methods such as cohort-based rolling starts, seasonal urgency, promotional/pricing urgency or exploding offers
Stresses that scarcity and urgency must be real/ethical (not phony)
Notes compliance caution for weight-loss outcome plus time claims or uses an action goal alternative
